headline: By 2035, more Muslims than Christians. 'It's the babies.'
summary: Pew Research Center projects Islam will pass Christianity as the world's largest religion by 2035: 2.57 billion Muslims to 2.52 billion Christians. Both faiths are growing, but Muslim women averaged 3.1 children against 2.5 for Christians. Conversion barely moves the numbers. Pew expects the US to lose its Christian majority by 2065.
cover_answer: Christianity today. Islam by 2035, because of babies.
table_question: Does the biggest group get to set the rules?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: Some families pray in a church, some in a mosque, some at home, some not at all. People who count the world say by 2035 there will be a few more Muslims than Christians, because Muslim families have more babies. Each group is about 2.5 billion people: counting them one a second would take 80 years. There's room for everyone.
5-7.why: Babies are a cause they can see. The rest is counting.
5-7.why_long: A seven-year-old reasons from what is in front of them, and the one thing in this story they can see is babies: more of them, so more people. The script gives them that and one picture of the size, 80 years of counting, then stops. Expect 'which one is right?' This is a count of people, and counting doesn't say who is right.

8-12.script: Pew, which counts the world's religions, says Islam passes Christianity by 2035, 2.57 billion to 2.52 billion. Muslim women average 3.1 children and Christian women 2.5, so Islam grows faster; switching barely moves it. Like two piggy banks fed $3 and $2.50 a week: the first catches up from behind.
8-12.why: Two piggy banks turn a birth rate into a race they can follow.
8-12.why_long: At eleven a child is working out chains of cause and effect, so the script runs one: more children per family, a faster-growing group, a new largest religion. The piggy banks make 3.1 against 2.5 a race they can follow. Expect 'does that mean Islam wins?' Pew counts people, and a count isn't a contest. Both faiths are growing.

13-17.script: Does it change anything if the world's largest religion changes? Pew says Islam passes Christianity by 2035, and Harvard's Gina Zurlo says many Christians are 'not happy'. Second: Pew says the US loses its Christian majority by 2065, mostly to no religion at all. Which number matters more?
13-17.why: Two numbers, one world and one country. Let them pick.
13-17.why_long: A fourteen-year-old can hold two true things: Islam becoming the largest faith, and the US becoming a place where no religion is the fastest-growing answer. The script hands them both, asks which matters; Kuhn's point is that argument is practised, not won. Expect 'why are people upset?' Zurlo says misunderstanding runs both ways.

5-7.a: Christianity today, with about 2.3 billion people. By 2035 it will be Islam, with 2.57 billion. Both are growing.

8-12.a: A count of people, not a contest. Both are growing; Islam faster.
Christians fall below half of US adults by 2065. No religion: 41% by 2070.

13-17.q: Why would anyone be upset about it?
13-17.a: Harvard's Gina Zurlo says both sides misunderstand each other.
Barely. Pew says the growth is births, not converts. 'It's the babies.'
